zh: 听这时又是『砰砰彭彭』好一阵，有的枪丢在外面箩筐，有的枪丢在里面箩筐，不过外面少，里面多。『是这样，』李勉林为左宗棠解释，『丢在外面的，没有修好，拿回去重修；丢在里面的，是修好了的。』左宗棠有些不大相信，『就这么看一眼、放一枪，就能听得出来？』他说∶『似乎有点不可思议。』『是！是有点不可思议，不过确实如此。』『我倒有点不明白。』左宗棠便趁空隙喊道∶『姚司务！姚司务！』那姚司务纹风不动，恍若未闻，李勉林赶紧又解释，『他重听，耳鼓让枪声震坏。平时说话，只看人的嘴。』接着他走上前去，拍一拍姚务的身后，让他下来。
en: Now came a rapid succession of cracks and thumps. Some rifles went into the outer basket and others into the inner one, though far fewer went into the outer. “Those in the outer basket have not been properly repaired and must go back,” Li Mianlin explained. “Those in the inner one are ready.” Zuo was not entirely convinced. “One glance and one shot, and he can tell by the sound? It seems scarcely credible.” “Indeed it does, but that is how he does it.” “There is something I do not understand.” During a pause, Zuo called, “Master Yao! Master Yao!” The old man did not stir, as though he had heard nothing. Li hastened to explain. “He is hard of hearing. Gunfire has damaged his eardrums. In ordinary conversation he watches people’s lips.” He stepped forward, tapped Yao on the back, and signalled him to come down.

zh: 『姚司务，』左宗棠问∶『你今年多大？』『六十六岁。』『你玩枪玩了少年了？』姚司务屈指算了一下∶『四十八年。』左宗棠也在心里略为算了一下说∶『这么说，你在道光那年就干这一行了？』『是。』『你跟谁学的？』『先是德国人，后来是英国人。』『喔！』左宗棠问∶『你说德国的枪好，还是英国的枪好？』『德国。』
en: “How old are you, Master Yao?” Zuo asked. “Sixty-six.” “How many years have you been handling guns?” Yao counted on his fingers. “Forty-eight.” Zuo made a quick calculation of his own. “Then you were already in this trade during the Daoguang reign?” “Yes.” “Who taught you?” “First a German, then an Englishman.” “And which guns do you think better, German or English?” “German.”

zh: 听这一说，左宗棠便回身去看，胡雪岩知道是找他，便从一大堆官员中挤上前去。『雪岩，』左宗棠问道∶『福克来了没有？』『没有。』胡雪岩问∶『大人有什么吩咐？我马上告诉他。』『我是要找一枝「温者斯得」的枪。』『呃，』胡雪岩答说∶『我已经分派给新兵，在用了。』『好、好！拿一枝来。』这枝枪是交到姚司务手里，问他见过没有？答说没有。不过他只略为看了一下，便转开一个螺丝，接着一样一样拆了下来，不过几分钟的工夫，一枝新枪成了一堆零件。这显出真工夫来了，左宗棠不能不服他，当下问道∶『这枪好不好？』那姚司务竟不回答，只看着李勉林。左宗棠不知是怎么回事；胡雪岩却看出来了，姚司务一说好，左宗棠说不定马上就会交代购买那一种。那一来，岂不断了采购委员的财路。因此，胡雪岩便说一句∶『只怕不见得好。』
en: Zuo turned to look behind him. Knowing whom he sought, Hu pushed forward through the crowd of officials. “Xueyan, has Focke come?” “No. Have you any instructions for him, Your Excellency? I shall pass them on at once.” “I want one of those Winchester rifles.” “I have already issued them to the recruits. They are using them.” “Good. Bring one here.” The rifle was placed in Yao’s hands, and he was asked whether he had seen one before. He had not. Yet after a brief examination, he turned a screw and began removing the parts one by one. In a few minutes, the new rifle lay in pieces. This was genuine skill, and Zuo could not withhold his admiration. “Is it a good rifle?” he asked. Yao gave no answer, merely looking at Li Mianlin. Zuo did not understand, but Hu did. If Yao pronounced it good, Zuo might immediately order rifles of that kind, cutting off the purchasing officers’ opportunities for profit. Hu therefore remarked, “Perhaps it is not so good.”

zh: 谁知李勉林恰好相反，连连说道∶『好，好，好得很。』表面彼此客气，实际上已等于短兵相接，也是彼此猜忌。本来江南制造局是李鸿章的禁脔，不管自造也好，外购也好，都轮不到胡雪岩来插手，所以他之说『怕不见得好』，便有不愿跟制造局『抢生意』的意味在内；反过来说，他如果要『抢生意』，唾手可得。这就使李勉林深深感到，劲敌当前，必须小心了。这笔买『温者斯得』来福枪的生意，自然还是归胡雪岩，但大发利市的却是福克。
en: Unexpectedly, Li took the opposite line. “Good, good—excellent!” he repeated. On the surface they were being polite; in reality, they were already crossing swords and regarding one another with suspicion. The Jiangnan Arsenal was Li Hongzhang’s exclusive preserve. Whether weapons were manufactured there or purchased abroad, Hu had no part in the business. His remark that the rifle might not be so good therefore signalled that he did not intend to compete for the arsenal’s trade. Conversely, if he chose to compete, that trade was within easy reach. Li Mianlin felt keenly that a formidable rival stood before him and that caution was necessary. The purchase of these Winchester rifles did, naturally, come Hu’s way. The man who profited handsomely, however, was Focke.

zh: 原来这种枪的在华代理权，属于福克的洋行，第一批进了五百枝，四处兜销，只卖去一百多，起初亦并未想到左宗棠，因为他知道西征军中来福枪极多，左宗棠甚至还送了一批给醇王，供神机营使用。及至听说胡雪岩要到上海，心想左宗棠的『小队』也许要用这种比较精良的新枪，送了二十枝当样品，估量着，即使能做到这笔生意，充其量也不过百把枝，库存还有一半，不知销场何在？哪知由胡雪岩转来的消息，说要买两千五百枝，预备分发江南各防营使用。福克喜出望外，却又发愁，因为能够供应的现贷，连个零头都不足。『胡先生，』福克透过古应春的翻译，向胡雪岩说∶『我拿库中存货先交，其余的，准备三个月内交齐；我回国去一趟，专门办这件事。
en: Focke’s firm held the Chinese agency for these rifles. Of the first five hundred imported, barely more than a hundred had been sold despite efforts in every direction. He had not initially thought of Zuo, knowing that the western armies already had many rifles; Zuo had even sent a consignment to Prince Chun for use by the Shenji Battalion. Hearing that Hu was coming to Shanghai, however, Focke thought Zuo’s personal detachment might need these superior new weapons and sent twenty as samples. Even if this produced an order, he expected no more than a hundred or so. Half his original stock would still remain, with no buyer in sight. Then word came through Hu: Zuo wanted two thousand five hundred, to be distributed among the various Jiangnan garrisons. Focke was delighted, but troubled as well. The goods available for immediate delivery did not amount even to the odd five hundred. “Mr Hu,” he said through Gu’s interpretation, “I shall deliver what I have in stock first and supply the rest within three months. I shall go home myself expressly to arrange it.”

zh: 胡雪碉便跟古应春商量，他亦看出李勉林对他深具戒心，认为不宜一开始就树敌，免得以后的障碍愈来愈多。这笔军火是左宗棠亲自交代，不能不办；正愁着李勉林会『吃味』，难得福克供应不足，恰好打消了这笔生意，避免得罪李勉林。他将他的意思告诉了给古应春，又说∶『我看就此推掉为妙。你跟他说，马上要用，要现货，没有现货就免谈了。』『这话他不会相认的。』古应春说∶『小爷叔在左大人面前讲话的分量，他不是不知道，哪一次买军火都是先送样品，看中意了再下定单，如今说全部都要现货，不是明明为难他？』『这话倒也是。』胡雪岩踌躇了一会说∶『这样，你叫他自己去看左大人。而且我们要避嫌疑，你叫他先到制造局去看李观察，请李观察带他去见左大人。生意成不成，看他自己的运气。』『这办法！行得通吗？』古应春不免怀疑，『我们犯不着把自己的路子，交给人家。』『不！现在他们怕我们防得厉害，犯不着为这点小事，做成个死对头。不如现在大方一点，以后办事反而顺手。』古应春心想，这是欲取姑予的手法，亦未尝不可用。两千五百枝枪的佣金，虽至少有五千佣金，别人看来是个大数目，但在胡雪岩眼中，却是小事；既然他要『大方』，就照他的意思办好了。
en: Hu discussed this with Gu. He too had seen how wary Li Mianlin was of him. It would be unwise to make an enemy at the outset and encounter increasing obstacles thereafter. Since Zuo had personally ordered these arms, he could hardly refuse to act; yet he feared Li’s resentment. Focke’s insufficient stock offered a convenient reason to abandon the transaction and avoid offending Li. He explained this to Gu. “We had better turn it down now. Tell him the rifles are needed immediately. We must have them in stock, or there is nothing to discuss.” “He will not accept that explanation. He knows how much influence you have with His Excellency. Arms purchases always begin with samples; if they are approved, an order follows. To insist now that the entire quantity be available at once would plainly be making difficulties for him.” “That is true.” Hu hesitated. “Then let him see His Excellency himself. To avoid any suspicion, have him first visit Intendant Li at the arsenal and ask Li to take him to His Excellency. Whether he secures the business will depend on his luck.” “Will that work?” Gu asked doubtfully. “We need not hand our own connections over to someone else.” “No. They are so afraid of us and so much on their guard that it would be foolish to make a sworn enemy over this small matter. A little generosity now will make future business easier.” Gu reflected that giving now in order to gain later was a legitimate tactic. The commission on two thousand five hundred rifles would be at least five thousand taels—a large sum to others, but a trifle to Hu. Since he wished to be generous, Gu would do as he asked.

zh: 但胡雪岩的顾虑与打算，福克是怎么样也无从知道的，因此一听古应春的话，大感困惑，多年合作得好好地，何以有这种见拒的态度？莫非胡雪岩在左宗棠面前，说话已经没有力量了，还是另有其他原因？当下率直向古应春发问。古应春当然不能跟他说实话，只说胡雪岩是尊重江南制造局。这话在福克半信半疑，他在华多年，官场中的情形，亦相当了解，向来是谁有办法，谁就可以争权夺利；权责并不分明，尊重更是假话。福克做事很老练，先去打听胡雪岩在左宗棠那里的『行情』，所得到的答复是绝未失宠。这一来，他就不能不怀疑，另有人在钻军火生意的路子，想取他而代之；胡雪岩是一种让他知难而退的态度。去问古应春，古应春绝口否认。这一下，福克释然了，中国官场不足跟外人道的花样很多，不必去多打听。反正自己仍旧抱定利益均沾的宗旨，将胡雪岩拉紧了，保持了多年合作的关系，总是不错的。
en: Focke could have no knowledge of Hu’s anxieties or calculations. He was bewildered by Gu’s message. After so many years of successful cooperation, why this rejection? Had Hu lost his influence with Zuo, or was there some other reason? He questioned Gu frankly. Unable to tell him the truth, Gu said only that Hu wished to respect the Jiangnan Arsenal’s position. Focke half believed him. After many years in China, he understood official life fairly well: whoever had the means could contend for power and profit. Authority and responsibility were ill-defined; talk of respect was still less credible. An experienced operator, Focke first inquired into Hu’s standing with Zuo and learned that he had certainly not fallen from favour. He therefore began to suspect that someone else was trying to supplant him in the arms trade, and that Hu meant to discourage him into withdrawing. Gu denied this absolutely. Focke then felt reassured. Chinese officialdom had many complications that could not be explained to foreigners; there was no need to investigate them all. In any event, he could not go wrong by holding to his principle of sharing profits, keeping Hu close, and preserving their longstanding cooperation.

zh: 于是福克便带了一名翻译到制造局求见李勉林。那时的官场，对洋人都是另眼看待，何况福克是上海洋商领袖之一，所以名刺一报进去，正在花厅中会客的李勉林，丢下他人，在签押房接见福克。动问来意，福克透过翻译说道∶『左大人要买两千五百枝温者斯得来福枪，可是我现货只有三百多枝，其余准三个月内交足。胡观察说不行，要我来见李观察，请你带我去见左大人当面谈。』听得这话，李勉林不免诧异，定购西洋军火，向来都是期货；目前内外无事，又不是打仗遇到劲敌，急需要精良武器才足以克制，何必一定非现货不可？仔细想一想，显然是胡雪岩不愿意经手这件事，但又为什么不愿意呢？唯一的缘故是左宗棠已非西征统帅，而是两江总督、南洋大臣，两个头衔中一『江』、『南』，就彰明较著地表明了，这一案应该由江南制造局主办。对于胡雪岩的能守分际，李勉林颇为佩服，胡雪岩的手腕很厉害，但还是『上路的』。
en: Focke therefore took an interpreter to the arsenal to see Li Mianlin. Officials gave foreigners special treatment in those days, and Focke was one of Shanghai’s leading foreign merchants. As soon as his card arrived, Li left the guests he was receiving in the garden reception room and met him in his private office. Asked his business, Focke explained through the interpreter: “His Excellency Zuo wishes to purchase two thousand five hundred Winchester rifles. I have only three hundred and some in stock, but can guarantee delivery of the rest within three months. Intendant Hu says that will not do and has sent me to ask you to take me to His Excellency so that I may discuss it with him in person.” Li was surprised. Foreign arms were normally ordered for future delivery. With no present disturbance at home or abroad, and no formidable enemy in battle requiring superior weapons urgently, why insist on immediate availability? Reflection made the answer plain: Hu did not wish to handle the purchase. Why not? There could be only one explanation. Zuo was no longer commander of the western expedition; he was governor-general of Liangjiang and commissioner for the Southern Ports. The “jiang” and “nan” in those titles unmistakably indicated that this business belonged to the Jiangnan Arsenal. Li admired Hu’s respect for the proper boundaries. Hu’s methods might be formidable, but he understood how things should be done.

zh: 当下欣然答说∶『可以、可以！左大人明天动身回江宁，我本来就要去见他；我们一起去好了。』于是约定当天下午三点钟，在天后宫行辕见面。到时候会齐李勉林先递书本谒见，然后找个谈话的空隙，说福克在外，等候接见，有事面禀。左宗棠已经接到胡雪岩的报告，认为胡雪岩所说，此案由江南制造局承办，一切签约、付款等等手续，都比较方便的看法不错，所以听得李勉林的话，立即接见福克。他跟福克很熟，也很欣赏福克的有条理，温言相接，颇假以词色；谈到买枪一事，也很爽快的答应了，先交若干现货，余数立定期限，陆续解交。价格方面，福克与李勉林细谈。
en: “Certainly!” Li answered readily. “His Excellency leaves for Jiangning tomorrow. I was going to see him in any case. We can go together.” They arranged to meet at three that afternoon at Zuo’s headquarters in the Temple of the Heavenly Empress. Once they had assembled there, Li sent in his card and was received first. At a suitable pause, he mentioned that Focke was waiting outside and had something to discuss in person. Hu had already reported to Zuo and argued that having the arsenal handle the transaction would make the contract, payments, and other formalities more convenient. Zuo approved this reasoning and immediately admitted Focke. He knew him well and appreciated his orderly way of doing things, so his greeting was warm and gracious. He also agreed readily to the proposed arrangement: the available rifles would be delivered first, and the remainder in instalments by a fixed deadline. Focke and Li were to settle the price between them.

zh: 『这两千五面枝枪是交绿营用的。』左宗棠交代李勉林∶『你收到枪，马上交给李朝斌好了。』李朝斌的官衔是江南提督，绿营的最高长官。『是。』『听说你要回国。』左宗棠转脸问福克∶『什么时候动身，什么时候回来？』『十天以后动身，两个月就回来。』『我现在要整顿水师；水师的利器，是鱼雷不是？』『是的。』『我想买一批鱼雷，你有没有？』『有、有。』福克答说∶『左大人知道的，东西洋各国凡有新出的利器，一定把样品跟说明书，送到我洋行里来的。尤其是这趟我回国，可以亲自打听到最新式的运了来。』『能不能连技师一起请了来。』『当然。凡是采购中国从前所没有的新式武器，一定由技师派来，教导如何演放。这是必有的规矩，不会错的。』『喔，你没有弄清我的意思，我是说能制造鱼雷的技师。』『那也有。』福克答说∶『不过要先看制造局，有没有能造鱼雷的机械。』『你跟李观察商量。』左宗棠又问∶『还有种「碰雷」，作何用处？』
en: “These two thousand five hundred rifles are for the Green Standard troops,” Zuo instructed Li. “As soon as you receive them, hand them over to Li Chaobin.” Li Chaobin was the Jiangnan commander-in-chief, the highest officer of the Green Standard forces. “Yes, Your Excellency.” Zuo turned to Focke. “I hear you are going home. When do you leave, and when will you return?” “In ten days. I shall be back in two months.” “I now intend to reorganize the navy. Torpedoes are an effective naval weapon, are they not?” “They are.” “I should like to purchase a consignment. Can you supply them?” “Certainly. As Your Excellency knows, whenever a new weapon appears in any country, East or West, samples and instructions are sent to my firm. On this journey home, I can personally inquire into the newest models and bring them out.” “Could you bring technicians as well?” “Of course. Whenever China buys a new weapon it has not used before, technicians are always sent to demonstrate its operation. That is an established practice; there will be no difficulty.” “You have misunderstood me. I mean technicians who can manufacture torpedoes.” “They can be found too, but we must first see whether the arsenal has suitable machinery.” “Discuss that with Intendant Li.” Zuo continued, “There is also something called a ‘contact mine.’ What is that used for?”

zh: 『是——』福克向翻译弄清楚了『碰雷』二字的意思，方始回答∶『那叫水雷，是专门为了防备对方兵舰用的。譬如一个港口，不愿意对方舰闯进来，就可以在港口海面上布下水雷，船一碰到就会爆炸。』『自己的船呢？』『自己的船，一样也会爆炸。』福克又说∶『水雷的威力很大，麻烦是不长眼睛，所以非遇到与外国交锋，打算断绝水路交通，不用水雷。』『事后呢？』『事后要清理。专门有种船叫扫雷艇。』『照此说来，这件事牵涉很广，暂作罢论，你只管替中国采购最新式的鱼雷好了。细节你跟李观察去商议。』『是！』看看没有话了，福七克在翻译示意之下，起身告辞。李勉林虽被留了下来，但从头到底没有能容他说一句话，内心万分不悦。
en: “It is—” Focke first clarified the term with his interpreter. “That is a naval mine, used specifically against enemy warships. For example, if you wish to keep their vessels out of a harbour, you can lay mines across its entrance. A ship touching one causes it to explode.” “What about our own ships?” “They would cause an explosion too. Mines are very powerful, but unfortunately they cannot distinguish friend from foe. They are therefore not used unless war with a foreign country makes it necessary to close the waterways.” “And afterwards?” “Afterwards they must be cleared. There is a special kind of vessel called a minesweeper.” “Then the matter has wide implications. We shall leave it aside for now. Simply obtain the latest torpedoes for China. Discuss the details with Intendant Li.” “Yes, Your Excellency.” There seemed nothing more to say. Prompted by the interpreter, Focke rose and took his leave. Li was asked to remain, but he had not been able to get a word into the entire conversation and was deeply displeased.

zh: 至于左宗棠将李勉林留了下来，是要谈半公半私的事。不过私事倒也不是他的个人之私，是为了曾国藩的小女婿聂规缉。原来曾国藩的欧阳夫人，共生三子六女。长子及五女，自幼夭折；在世的有两子五女，长子纪泽，文章政事俱是第一流，而且由自修而通英文，为国藩所看重，后来袭封侯爵，以钦差大臣出使西洋，与郭嵩焘都是真正懂洋务的大才。次子纪鸿中举以后，会试一直不利；曾国藩也知道『场中莫论文』，考试要碰运气，但功名这念，横亘胸中；期望亦未免过切，总说他的次子不用功。偏偏运气也真坏，直到曾国藩去世，始终是个举人，以后也一直没有能够中进士，与长兄相较，境遇大不相同，以至于在京郁郁以终，身后还是左宗棠替他料理的。
en: Zuo had kept Li behind to discuss something partly public and partly private. The private interest was not his own, however; it concerned Zeng Guofan’s youngest son-in-law, Nie Guiji. Zeng’s wife, Madam Ouyang, had borne three sons and six daughters. The first son and fifth daughter died in childhood, leaving two sons and five daughters. The elder surviving son, Jize, excelled both in letters and in public affairs. He had also taught himself English, which greatly pleased his father. Later he inherited the marquisate and went to the West as an imperial envoy. He and Guo Songtao were men of exceptional ability who truly understood foreign affairs. The younger son, Jihong, passed the provincial examination but repeatedly failed at the metropolitan level. Zeng knew that literary merit did not guarantee success in the examination hall and that luck played a part. Yet official distinction remained an obsession, and his expectations were too pressing; he constantly accused his younger son of not studying hard enough. Jihong’s luck was indeed poor. When Zeng died, he was still only a provincial graduate, and he never subsequently obtained the metropolitan degree. His circumstances differed so greatly from his elder brother’s that he died despondent in the capital. It was Zuo who attended to his affairs after his death.

zh: 比起曾纪鸿来，他的姐妹们的境遇，又更不如他了，有的婆婆太凶，有的丈夫没出息。曾国藩持家极严，说他见过许多名门之女，贪恋母家富，往往不肯在夫家尽子妇之道，到后来都无好结果，因此他的女儿虽都遇人不淑，但因曾国藩不许她们归宁，只好在夫家受罪，个个都是终日以泪洗面。其中四小姐嫁得不错，偏又青年守寡，所以曾国藩生前常说，他的『坦运不佳』。六小姐是取小的女儿，湖南人称为『满小姐』，名叫曾纪芬，她是曾国藩去世后才嫁的。本来由她叔叔『九帅』作媒，许婚于衡山聂家，定在同治十一年出阁。不意就在这年二月初，曾国藩中风殁于两江总督任上；到得服满已是光绪年间。
en: Compared with Jihong, his sisters fared worse still. Some had fierce mothers-in-law; others had worthless husbands. Zeng governed his household strictly. He said he had seen many daughters of prominent families who clung to the wealth of their parents’ homes and neglected their duties as wives and daughters-in-law, and that none had come to a good end. Although his own daughters had made unfortunate marriages, he would not permit them to return home. They had to endure their misery with their husbands’ families, spending their days in tears. The fourth daughter had married well, only to be widowed young. Zeng often said that his luck in sons-in-law was poor. The sixth daughter, his youngest—what Hunan people called the “last little miss”—was Zeng Jifen. She married only after his death. Her uncle, Ninth Marshal Zeng, had arranged the match with the Nie family of Hengshan, and the wedding was set for the eleventh year of Tongzhi. But early in the second month of that year, Zeng suffered a stroke and died in office as governor-general of Liangjiang. By the time mourning ended, the Guangxu reign had begun.

zh: 曾纪芬的夫婿聂规缉，字芸台，他家是衡山世家，先世以行善出名。但聂规缉却连个举人都没有考上，以致于只能混个小差使；他有个姐夫为先前的两江总督刘坤一委为『筹防局总办』，聂规缉单身跟到江宁，在筹防局当差，只得八两银子的车马费，但却要接眷；原来聂规缉到了江宁，才知道曾国藩真是门生故吏满天下，将他妻子以『曾文正的满小姐』这个『头衔』搬出来，在裙带上着实能拖出来一点好处，这就是他接眷的打算。果然，曾纪芬照她丈夫的嘱咐，由湖南坐船经武昌时，特为去拜见湖广总督李瀚章的夫人，稍为谈一谈丈夫的境况，聂规缉立即被委为湖南督运局驻江宁的委员，月支津贴五十两，日子过得很舒服了。
en: Jifen’s husband, Nie Guiji, whose courtesy name was Yuntai, belonged to an established Hengshan family long known for charitable works. He had failed even to gain the provincial degree and could obtain only minor employment. One of his brothers-in-law had been made director of the Defence Preparations Bureau by the former governor-general of Liangjiang, Liu Kunyi. Nie followed him to Jiangning alone and took a position in the bureau, receiving only eight taels for transport expenses. Yet he wanted to bring his wife there. Once in Jiangning, he had discovered how widely Zeng’s former pupils and subordinates were dispersed. By presenting his wife under the title “Lord Wenzheng Zeng’s youngest daughter,” he could extract considerable benefit from her connections. That was why he wished her to join him. Following his instructions, Jifen made a special call on the wife of Li Hanzhang, governor-general of Huguang, when her boat from Hunan passed through Wuchang. She said a little about her husband’s circumstances. Nie was promptly appointed the Hunan Transport Supervision Bureau’s representative in Jiangning, with a monthly allowance of fifty taels. Life became quite comfortable.

zh: 及至左宗棠接刘坤一的手，到了江宁不久，便将曾纪芬接到总督衙门叙旧，曾国藩生在嘉庆十六年辛未；左宗棠生在壬申小一岁，因而以叔父自居。左宗棠在曾国荃克江宁后，与曾国藩失和，有三四年不通音问，但当左示棠奉命西征，曾国藩命湘军刘松山相助，大为得力，这使得左宗棠大为感动，而况平生功名，关键所在是曾国藩知道他的才具，派他独当一面收复浙江，与曾氏兄弟同时封爵。拜相封侯，位极人臣，饮水思源，亦不能不感激曾国藩；所以表面上倔强如昔，仍旧处处要批评曾国藩，私底下的态度，却已大为改变，曾国藩殁后，他致送的挽联，道是∶『谋国之忠，知人之明，自愧不如元辅』，这等于认输，以左宗棠的性情来说，是很难得的事。
en: Soon after succeeding Liu Kunyi at Jiangning, Zuo invited Jifen to the governor-general’s residence to talk over old times. Zeng had been born in the xinwei year, the sixteenth of Jiaqing; Zuo, born in the following renshen year, was a year younger and assumed the role of her uncle. After Zeng Guoquan captured Jiangning, Zuo and Zeng Guofan had quarrelled and ceased corresponding for three or four years. But when Zuo was ordered to campaign in the west, Zeng sent Liu Songshan of the Xiang Army to assist him. His help proved invaluable and deeply moved Zuo. Moreover, the decisive opportunity in Zuo’s career had come when Zeng recognized his ability and entrusted him with independent command to recover Zhejiang, enabling him to receive a noble title alongside the Zeng brothers. Having risen to the highest ministerial honours and a marquisate, Zuo could hardly forget the source of his good fortune. Outwardly he remained as stubborn as ever, criticizing Zeng at every turn, but privately his attitude had changed greatly. When Zeng died, Zuo sent a funeral couplet whose first line read: “In loyalty to the state and discernment of men, I acknowledge myself inferior to the chief minister.” This amounted to conceding defeat—an uncommon act for a man of Zuo’s temperament.

zh: 至于照应曾国藩的后人，是为了要证实他的挽联中的下一句∶『同心若金，攻错若石，相期无负平生』，与曾国藩是为国事而争，私交丝毫无损。特别是老年人，往往有一种将朋友的女儿看作自己掌上珠的通性，爱屋及乌，对聂规缉亦就另眼相看，派了他营务处的差使，每天中午会食，一定找聂规缉；对他的肯说实话、留心西学，颇为赞许，有心要培植他。这回左宗棠出省阅兵，聂规缉作随员，李勉林跟他是熟人，左宗棠故意相问∶『勉林，你跟聂芸台熟不熟？』李勉林各州兴锐，早年曾替曾国藩办过粮台，当即答道∶『他是曾文正的满女婿，我当然很熟。』『那就再好没有。我看你也很忙，我想派他来当你的会办。』
en: His care for Zeng’s descendants was intended to bear out the couplet’s second line: “Our shared purpose was firm as metal; our corrections of each other, a whetstone; may neither betray the hopes of a lifetime.” Their disagreements concerned affairs of state and had never impaired their private friendship. Elderly men, moreover, often regarded a friend’s daughter as a precious child of their own. Zuo’s affection extended to Nie. He appointed him to the military administration office and invariably summoned him to share the midday meal. He approved of Nie’s willingness to speak honestly and his interest in Western learning, and intended to foster his career. Nie accompanied him on this tour of military inspection outside the province. Li Mianlin knew the young man, and Zuo deliberately asked, “Mianlin, do you know Nie Yuntai well?” Li, whose personal name was Xingrui, had once managed military supplies for Zeng. “He is Lord Wenzheng’s youngest son-in-law,” he replied. “Of course I know him well.” “Excellent. You seem very busy. I should like to appoint him your assistant director.”
